title: Track Pairs Filling Whole Minutes
statement: A playlist has track lengths in seconds, secs[i]. Count the pairs of positions i < j whose combined length secs[i] + secs[j] is a whole number of minutes, that is, divisible by 60.

examples.why: 45 pairs with 75 (120) and with 15 (60). 105 pairs with 75 (180) and with 15 (120). 45 + 105 = 150 is not a whole minute.
Every pair works: tracks with remainder 0 pair with each other. They are their own partners, which is easy to miss.
Remainder 30 also pairs with itself: 3 tracks give 3 pairs, not 3 × 3.

hints: Only the remainder of each length mod 60 matters. What remainder does a partner of a 45-second track need?
A track with remainder r pairs with any earlier track whose remainder is (60 − r) mod 60. Keep a count for each of the 60 remainders.
Walk left to right: add the count of the needed remainder to the answer, then record the current track's remainder. The mod 60 on the needed value makes remainder 0 pair with 0.

explain.intuition:
Whole minutes only care about the seconds that spill over, so reduce every length to secs[i] % 60. Now a pair works when the two remainders add up to 0 or 60. This is two-sum with a twist: instead of an exact target, you look for the complementary remainder.

Count as you go. When you reach a track, every earlier track with the matching remainder forms one pair with it, so add how many such tracks you have seen. Counting only earlier tracks makes each pair count once, including pairs of two remainder-0 or two remainder-30 tracks.
steps: For each track, let r = secs[i] % 60 and need = (60 − r) % 60.
pitfalls: Using 60 − r without the final % 60. For r = 0 it looks for remainder 60, which never exists.
Counting all pairs of remainder groups after the fact as count[r] × count[60 − r] for every r. Remainders 0 and 30 pair with themselves and need n(n − 1)/2, and the other pairs get counted twice.
Pairing a track with itself. Only earlier tracks count.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Two nested loops over i < j, test whether the sum is divisible by 60.

solutions.title: Remainder counts in one pass
solutions.idea: For each track, add how many earlier tracks have the complementary remainder, then record this track's remainder.

followups: Count triples whose total is divisible by 60.
Instead of a count, return the pair whose total is the longest whole number of minutes.
